_source: Default bindings (issue #113; traced in wiki document 137, the shape is the engine's PlayerControls). Three sets, as the original keeps them in its 66-halfword registry block: one_player, two_player_1, two_player_2. Each control lists its bindings, all live and ORed (FUN_0041b890): a key (Godot's name), an input action, or 'joy:<code>', one of the original's 24 joystick input codes (FUN_0041cb00). two_player_1 / two_player_2 are the original's defaults (FUN_0041c990 keys: W S A D, Q E, H J K and keypad 8 5 4 6, 7 9, - + Enter; FUN_0041ca40 joystick codes). one_player keeps the original's joystick defaults, but its keys are a PORT CHOICE (user, 2026-10-12): the port's own keys on the same three-button scheme, the arrows and ui_accept (Space, Enter) as A, Z as B, X as C, Q and E as the shoulders; the original's one-player keys are the same as two_player_1's. 'editor' lays out the Settings' Controls screen (ControlsScreen, issue #121, document 141) as CONFIG.BIN's dialogs 129 'Configuration - 1 Player' and 130 'Configuration - 2 Player': the row labels (ids 0x43c-0x444, in the dialog's order), the headings (ACTION, KEY, JOYSTICK / PLAYER 1, PLAYER 2, KEY, JOY), and the joystick list's entries (the combo boxes' initial strings, '*NONE*' then ' 1 Up' ... ' 2POV Down', trimmed). The joystick names are given by code from their meaning (stick, button A-D = buttons 1-4, POV = hat); how CONFIG.BIN turns a list index into a code was not traced.
